chapterTitle: The River of Life and the Final Invitation
themeTitle: “Yes, I Come Quickly.” Amen! Yes, Come, Lord Jesus

scripture.text: He showed me a river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb,
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ἔδειξέν μοι ποταμὸν ὕδατος ζωῆς λαμπρὸν ὡς κρύσταλλον, “He showed me a river of water of life, clear as crystal” — ζωή, from the life family: the life of God Himself. Eden had a river that watered the garden; Ezekiel saw a river flowing from the temple, giving life wherever it went. ἐκπορευόμενον ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἀρνίου, “proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb” — one throne, shared by God and the Lamb (ἀρνίον, from the lamb family). Life flows from God's rule. Jesus spoke of living water — the Holy Spirit (John 7:38–39).

scripture.text: in the middle of its street. On this side of the river and on that was the tree of life, bearing twelve kinds of fruits, yielding its fruit every month. The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.
scripture.understanding: ἐν μέσῳ τῆς πλατείας αὐτῆς, “in the middle of its street” — the river runs down the city's main street. καὶ τοῦ ποταμοῦ ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ξύλον ζωῆς, “On this side of the river and on that was the tree of life” — ξύλον; ζωή, from the life family: the tree that was barred after the fall (Genesis 3:24), promised to the overcomer (2:7), now open to all. ποιοῦν καρποὺς δώδεκα, κατὰ μῆνα ἕκαστον ἀποδιδοῦν τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῦ, “bearing twelve kinds of fruits, yielding its fruit every month” — μήν, from the time family: endless abundance, no barren season. καὶ τὰ φύλλα τοῦ ξύλου εἰς θεραπείαν τῶν ἐθνῶν, “The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations” — θεραπεία, healing (our ‘therapy’): the wounds of history between nations healed.

scripture.text: There will be no curse any more. The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will serve him.
scripture.understanding: καὶ πᾶν κατάθεμα οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι, “There will be no curse any more” — κατάθεμα: the curse pronounced in Eden on the ground and on human life (Genesis 3:17) is lifted forever; Zechariah promised ‘there will be no more curse’ (Zechariah 14:11). καὶ ὁ θρόνος τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ ἀρνίου ἐν αὐτῇ ἔσται, “The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it” — ἀρνίον, from the lamb family. καὶ οἱ δοῦλοι αὐτοῦ λατρεύσουσιν αὐτῷ, “and his servants will serve him” — δοῦλος and λατρεύω, two members of the servant family: δοῦλος, a bondservant who belongs to his master; λατρεύω, priestly service in worship. God's slaves are His priests (7:15).

scripture.text: They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὄψονται τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, “They will see his face” — ὁράω, from the see family. The deepest longing of the Bible: Moses was told no one could see God's face and live; the psalmist prayed to see it; Jesus promised the pure in heart ‘shall see God’. Now it is granted. καὶ τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν, “and his name will be on their foreheads” — the seal of 7:3 and 14:1: they belong to Him wholly, like the high priest who wore ‘HOLY TO THE LORD’ on his forehead.

scripture.text: There will be no night, and they need no lamp light; for the Lord God will illuminate them. They will reign forever and ever.
scripture.understanding: καὶ νὺξ οὐκ ἔσται ἔτι, “There will be no night” — and therefore no fear and no darkness. καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν χρείαν φωτὸς λύχνου καὶ φωτὸς ἡλίου, ὅτι κύριος ὁ θεὸς φωτίσει ἐπ᾽ αὐτούς, “and they need no lamp light; for the Lord God will illuminate them” — φωτίζω: God Himself is their light. καὶ βασιλεύσουσιν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, “They will reign forever and ever” — βασιλεύω; αἰών, from the time family and the world family. The book that began with a persecuted church ends with God's servants reigning forever.

scripture.text: He said to me, “These words are faithful and true. The Lord God of the spirits of the prophets sent his angel to show to his bondservants the things which must happen soon.”
scripture.understanding: Καὶ εἶπέν μοι· Οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι πιστοὶ καὶ ἀληθινοί, “He said to me, ‘These words are faithful and true’” — λόγος, from the word family: the epilogue (vv. 6–21) begins by affirming that everything in the book is trustworthy (21:5). καὶ ὁ κύριος ὁ θεὸς τῶν πνευμάτων τῶν προφητῶν ἀπέστειλεν τὸν ἄγγελον αὐτοῦ, “The Lord God of the spirits of the prophets sent his angel” — δεῖξαι τοῖς δούλοις αὐτοῦ ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι ἐν τάχει, “to show to his bondservants the things which must happen soon” — δοῦλος, from the servant family; the words of 1:1, bringing the book full circle.

scripture.text: “Behold, I come quickly. Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.”
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ταχύ, “Behold, I come quickly” — ταχύ, soon, without delay, suddenly. The first of three ‘I come quickly’ in this chapter (vv. 7, 12, 20). Two thousand years later, ‘quickly’ reminds us that His coming is always near and always sudden, and that ‘one day is with the Lord as a thousand years’ (2 Peter 3:8). μακάριος ὁ τηρῶν τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου, “Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book” — the sixth blessing, echoing the first (1:3); τηρέω, from the hold family; λόγος, from the word family; βιβλίον, from the book family.

scripture.text: Now I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. When I heard and saw, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who had shown me these things.
scripture.understanding: Κἀγὼ Ἰωάννης ὁ ἀκούων καὶ βλέπων ταῦτα, “Now I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things” — βλέπω, from the see family: the eyewitness signature, like 1 John 1:1. καὶ ὅτε ἤκουσα καὶ ἔβλεψα, ἔπεσα προσκυνῆσαι ἔμπροσθεν τῶν ποδῶν τοῦ ἀγγέλου τοῦ δεικνύοντός μοι ταῦτα, “When I heard and saw, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who had shown me these things” — βλέπω again; the same mistake as 19:10. Even after all he has seen, John is tempted to worship the messenger rather than God.

scripture.text: He said to me, “See you don’t do it! I am a fellow bondservant with you and with your brothers, the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book. Worship God.”
scripture.understanding: καὶ λέγει μοι· Ὅρα μή, “He said to me, ‘See you don’t do it!’” — ὁράω, from the see family. σύνδουλός σού εἰμι καὶ τῶν ἀδελφῶν σου τῶν προφητῶν καὶ τῶν τηρούντων τοὺς λόγους τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου, “I am a fellow bondservant with you and with your brothers, the prophets, and with those who keep the words of this book” — τηρέω, from the hold family; λόγος, from the word family; βιβλίον, from the book family. τῷ θεῷ προσκύνησον, “Worship God” — the message of the whole book in two words, repeated.

scripture.text: He said to me, “Don’t seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is at hand.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ λέγει μοι· Μὴ σφραγίσῃς τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου, “He said to me, ‘Don’t seal up the words of the prophecy of this book’” — σφραγίζω; λόγος, from the word family; βιβλίον, from the book family. Daniel was told to seal his book until the time of the end (Daniel 12:4); John is told the opposite. The book is open, meant for the churches now. ὁ καιρὸς γὰρ ἐγγύς ἐστιν, “for the time is at hand” — καιρός, from the time family: the decisive season, as in 1:3.

scripture.text: He who acts unjustly, let him act unjustly still. He who is filthy, let him be filthy still. He who is righteous, let him do righteousness still. He who is holy, let him be holy still.”
scripture.understanding: ὁ ἀδικῶν ἀδικησάτω ἔτι, καὶ ὁ ῥυπαρὸς ῥυπανθήτω ἔτι, “He who acts unjustly, let him act unjustly still. He who is filthy, let him be filthy still” — not an encouragement to sin, but a solemn warning: the time is short; character is becoming fixed. καὶ ὁ δίκαιος δικαιοσύνην ποιησάτω ἔτι, καὶ ὁ ἅγιος ἁγιασθήτω ἔτι, “He who is righteous, let him do righteousness still. He who is holy, let him be holy still” — ἅγιος and ἁγιάζω, two members of the holy family: holy in status, and being made holy in practice. As Daniel heard, ‘the wicked will do wickedly... but those who are wise will understand.’ Keep going in the way you are going — if it is the right way.

scripture.text: “Behold, I come quickly. My reward is with me, to repay to each man according to his work.
scripture.understanding: Ἰδοὺ ἔρχομαι ταχύ, “Behold, I come quickly” — ταχύ, the second time. καὶ ὁ μισθός μου μετ᾽ ἐμοῦ, “My reward is with me” — μισθός, wages: Isaiah's promise, ‘Behold, his reward is with him.’ ἀποδοῦναι ἑκάστῳ ὡς τὸ ἔργον ἐστὶν αὐτοῦ, “to repay to each man according to his work” — ἔργον, from the work family, singular: a person's whole life's work, the fruit of faith or unbelief (20:12).

scripture.text: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End.
scripture.understanding: ἐγὼ τὸ Ἄλφα καὶ τὸ Ὦ, ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος, ἡ ἀρχὴ καὶ τὸ τέλος, “I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End” — Jesus now claims all three titles that God used of Himself (1:8; 21:6; Isaiah 44:6). ἀρχή, from the power family: the source and ruler; τέλος, from the perfect family: the goal and completion. The clearest statement in the book that Jesus is God.

scripture.text: Blessed are those who do his commandments, that they may have the right to the tree of life, and may enter in by the gates into the city.
scripture.understanding: Μακάριοι οἱ ποιοῦντες τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ, “Blessed are those who do his commandments” — the seventh and last blessing. The WEB follows manuscripts reading ‘do his commandments’; the oldest read πλύνοντες τὰς στολὰς αὐτῶν, ‘wash their robes’ (7:14) — in Greek the two phrases look and sound very alike. ἵνα ἔσται ἡ ἐξουσία αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τὸ ξύλον τῆς ζωῆς, “that they may have the right to the tree of life” — ἐξουσία, from the power family: the authority, the right of access; ζωή, from the life family. καὶ τοῖς πυλῶσιν εἰσέλθωσιν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, “and may enter in by the gates into the city” — the pearl gates (21:21), always open.

scripture.text: Outside are the dogs, the sorcerers, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood.
scripture.understanding: ἔξω οἱ κύνες, “Outside are the dogs” — κύων: a term of contempt for the shamelessly impure (Philippians 3:2). καὶ οἱ φάρμακοι καὶ οἱ πόρνοι καὶ οἱ φονεῖς καὶ οἱ εἰδωλολάτραι, “the sorcerers, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters” — the list of 21:8. καὶ πᾶς φιλῶν καὶ ποιῶν ψεῦδος, “and everyone who loves and practices falsehood” — φιλέω, from the love family: to be fond of, to have a liking for, as distinct from ἀγαπάω, the love of commitment. Those who are fond of the lie — who love the beast's world — stay outside the city of truth. Even now, the gates are open to any who will wash their robes.

scripture.text: I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you for the assemblies. I am the root and the offspring of David; the Bright and Morning Star.”
scripture.understanding: Ἐγὼ Ἰησοῦς ἔπεμψα τὸν ἄγγελόν μου μαρτυρῆσαι ὑμῖν ταῦτα ἐπὶ ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις, “I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you for the assemblies” — μαρτυρέω, from the witness family. The whole book is for the churches. ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ῥίζα καὶ τὸ γένος Δαυίδ, “I am the root and the offspring of David” — both the source of David's line (as God) and its descendant (as man). ὁ ἀστὴρ ὁ λαμπρὸς ὁ πρωϊνός, “the Bright and Morning Star” — ἀστήρ; πρωϊνός: the star that rises before dawn, announcing the new day. Balaam foresaw ‘a star out of Jacob’; Jesus promised to give the overcomer ‘the morning star’ (2:28) — Himself.

scripture.text: The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” He who hears, let him say, “Come!” He who is thirsty, let him come. He who desires, let him take the water of life freely.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ ἡ νύμφη λέγουσιν· Ἔρχου, “The Spirit and the bride say, ‘Come!’” — νύμφη: the church, moved by the Spirit, calls to Christ: ‘Come!’ καὶ ὁ ἀκούων εἰπάτω· Ἔρχου, “He who hears, let him say, ‘Come!’” — every hearer joins the prayer. καὶ ὁ διψῶν ἐρχέσθω, “He who is thirsty, let him come” — and the call turns outward to the world: Christ's invitation to everyone. ὁ θέλων λαβέτω ὕδωρ ζωῆς δωρεάν, “He who desires, let him take the water of life freely” — ζωή, from the life family; δωρεάν, as a free gift (21:6). The last invitation of the Bible is free and open to all.

scripture.text: I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book, if anyone adds to them, may God add to him the plagues which are written in this book.
scripture.understanding: Μαρτυρῶ ἐγὼ παντὶ τῷ ἀκούοντι τοὺς λόγους τῆς προφητείας τοῦ βιβλίου τούτου, “I testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book” — μαρτυρέω, from the witness family; λόγος, from the word family; βιβλίον, from the book family. ἐάν τις ἐπιθῇ ἐπ᾽ αὐτά, ἐπιθήσει ὁ θεὸς ἐπ᾽ αὐτὸν τὰς πληγὰς τὰς γεγραμμένας ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τούτῳ, “if anyone adds to them, may God add to him the plagues which are written in this book” — ἐπιτίθημι; βιβλίον, from the book family. Like Moses' warning in Deuteronomy, it protects the message from distortion — the very sin of the false prophets.

scripture.text: If anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, may God take away his part from the tree of life, and out of the holy city, which are written in this book.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐάν τις ἀφέλῃ ἀπὸ τῶν λόγων τοῦ βιβλίου τῆς προφητείας ταύτης, “If anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy” — ἀφαιρέω, to remove; λόγος, from the word family; βιβλίον, from the book family. ἀφελεῖ ὁ θεὸς τὸ μέρος αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ ξύλου τῆς ζωῆς καὶ ἐκ τῆς πόλεως τῆς ἁγίας, “may God take away his part from the tree of life, and out of the holy city” — ζωή, from the life family; ἅγιος, from the holy family. Some manuscripts read ‘the book of life’. The warning is first about this book, but it reflects how seriously God guards all His word.

scripture.text: He who testifies these things says, “Yes, I come quickly.” Amen! Yes, come, Lord Jesus.
scripture.understanding: Λέγει ὁ μαρτυρῶν ταῦτα, “He who testifies these things says” — μαρτυρέω, from the witness family: Jesus, the faithful witness (1:5). Ναί, ἔρχομαι ταχύ, “Yes, I come quickly” — ταχύ, the third and final time. Ἀμήν, ἔρχου κύριε Ἰησοῦ, “Amen! Yes, come, Lord Jesus” — the church's answer: the Aramaic prayer of the first Christians, ‘Maranatha’ (1 Corinthians 16:22). The last prayer of the Bible.

scripture.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with all the saints. Amen.
scripture.understanding: Ἡ χάρις τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ μετὰ πάντων τῶν ἁγίων, “The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with all the saints” — χάρις, grace; ἅγιος, from the holy family (many manuscripts read simply ‘with all’). A book of thunder, beasts and bowls ends like a letter, with grace. Ἀμήν, “Amen” — the last word of the Bible: so let it be.

visualMeditations.title: The River and the Tree
visualMeditations.image: Picture a river as clear as crystal flowing from the throne of God and the Lamb, down the golden street of the city. On both banks grows the tree of life, heavy with twelve kinds of fruit, a new crop every month; and people from every nation rest under it, its leaves healing every old wound.
visualMeditations.meaning: “He showed me a river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb... On this side of the river and on that was the tree of life... The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations” (vv. 1–2). The garden lost in Genesis is restored and surpassed in Revelation.

visualMeditations.title: They Will See His Face
visualMeditations.image: Picture a vast crowd of God's servants — no curse, no night, no lamps needed — and every face turned upward, looking at the One on the throne. For the first time, they see His face; and His name shines on their foreheads.
visualMeditations.meaning: “They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads. There will be no night... for the Lord God will illuminate them. They will reign forever and ever” (vv. 4–5). Every longing of the human heart is fulfilled in seeing God.

visualMeditations.title: The Morning Star
visualMeditations.image: Picture the darkest hour of the night, just before dawn. Then, low on the horizon, one star appears, brighter than all the others, announcing that the night is almost over and the day is coming.
visualMeditations.meaning: “I, Jesus... I am the root and the offspring of David; the Bright and Morning Star” (v. 16). Whatever darkness you are in, Jesus is the sign that morning is coming.

visualMeditations.title: Come
visualMeditations.image: Picture the church, the bride, standing at the edge of history, looking toward the horizon, and the Spirit within her crying, ‘Come!’ Then she turns to the thirsty crowds of the world and calls to them too: ‘Come! Take the water of life — it's free.’ And from heaven comes the answer: ‘Yes, I come quickly.’
visualMeditations.meaning: “The Spirit and the bride say, ‘Come!’... He who desires, let him take the water of life freely” (v. 17). “He who testifies these things says, ‘Yes, I come quickly.’ Amen! Yes, come, Lord Jesus” (v. 20).

structure.label: The River and the Tree (v. 1-5)
structure.body: The angel shows John the river of the water of life flowing from the throne of God and the Lamb down the city's street; the tree of life grows on both banks, bearing fruit every month, its leaves for the healing of the nations; there is no more curse; God's servants will worship Him, see His face and bear His name, with no night, for the Lord God is their light, and they will reign forever.

structure.label: These Words Are Faithful and True (v. 6-11)
structure.body: The angel affirms that the words are trustworthy; Jesus says, ‘I come quickly’ and blesses those who keep the prophecy; John falls to worship the angel and is told to worship God; he is told not to seal up the book, for the time is near; let the unjust and the righteous continue in their ways.

structure.label: Jesus' Final Words (v. 12-16)
structure.body: Jesus says He is coming soon with His reward for each person's work; He is the Alpha and Omega, the First and Last, the Beginning and End; blessed are those who wash their robes and may enter the city; outside are the dogs and all who love falsehood; Jesus has sent His angel to the churches; He is the root and offspring of David, the bright morning star.

structure.label: Invitation, Warning and Benediction (v. 17-21)
structure.body: The Spirit and the bride say, ‘Come’; let the thirsty come and take the water of life freely; a warning against adding to or taking away from the prophecy; Jesus says, ‘Yes, I am coming quickly’; the church answers, ‘Amen. Come, Lord Jesus’; the grace of the Lord Jesus be with all.

sections.heading: Paradise Restored
paragraphs: The Bible begins in a garden with a river and a tree of life, and ends in a city with a river and a tree of life. “He showed me a river of water of life, clear as crystal, proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb, in the middle of its street. On this side of the river and on that was the tree of life” (vv. 1–2). What was lost in Genesis 3 is restored — and more than restored: a garden has become a garden-city, the home of a redeemed humanity from every nation.

The tree bears fruit every month, and “The leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations” (v. 2). The wounds between peoples — wars, hatreds, injustices — are healed. “There will be no curse any more” (v. 3). The curse that fell on the ground and on human life after the first sin is lifted forever.

And at the heart of it all: “The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and his servants will serve him. They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads” (vv. 3–4). Moses was told that no one could see God's face and live. Paul wrote, “For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face” (1 Corinthians 13:12). Jesus promised, “Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God” (Matthew 5:8). This is the beatific vision — the end and joy of all things. “They will reign forever and ever” (v. 5).

sections.heading: Faithful and True Words
paragraphs: The book now closes as it began. “These words are faithful and true” (v. 6); the angel was sent “to show to his bondservants the things which must happen soon” (v. 6), the words of 1:1. “Behold, I come quickly. Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book” (v. 7) echoes the first blessing (1:3). The whole book is framed by blessing on those who keep it.

Once again John falls before the angel, and once again he is stopped: “See you don’t do it! I am a fellow bondservant with you... Worship God” (v. 9). If the beloved apostle, after seeing all this, could be tempted to worship the wrong thing, so can we. The whole message of Revelation could be summed up in those two words: Worship God.

Unlike Daniel, John is told, “Don’t seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is at hand” (v. 10). Then comes a sobering word: “He who acts unjustly, let him act unjustly still... He who is holy, let him be holy still” (v. 11). This is not permission to sin, but a warning that the time is short and character is becoming fixed. The direction you are going now is the direction you will go.

sections.heading: The First and the Last
paragraphs: Jesus speaks directly: “Behold, I come quickly. My reward is with me, to repay to each man according to his work. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End” (vv. 12–13). He takes to Himself every title that God claimed in the book (1:8; 21:6). There is no clearer statement in Revelation that Jesus is fully God.

“Blessed are those who do his commandments, that they may have the right to the tree of life, and may enter in by the gates into the city” (v. 14). The oldest manuscripts read ‘Blessed are those who wash their robes’ — the robes washed white in the Lamb's blood (7:14). Either way, the way into the city is through the Lamb. “Outside are the dogs, the sorcerers, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters, and everyone who loves and practices falsehood” (v. 15). The gates are always open, but those who prefer the lie stay outside.

“I, Jesus, have sent my angel to testify these things to you for the assemblies. I am the root and the offspring of David; the Bright and Morning Star” (v. 16). He is both David's Lord and David's Son (Matthew 22:42–45). And He is the morning star that rises in the darkest hour before dawn. Peter wrote of the prophetic word as “a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns, and the morning star arises in your hearts” (2 Peter 1:19).

sections.heading: Come
paragraphs: The last invitation of the Bible: “The Spirit and the bride say, ‘Come!’ He who hears, let him say, ‘Come!’ He who is thirsty, let him come. He who desires, let him take the water of life freely” (v. 17). The church, moved by the Spirit, cries to Christ to come; and then turns to the world and cries to everyone who is thirsty to come. The water of life is free. Jesus said to the Samaritan woman, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water” (John 4:10).

Then a solemn warning against adding to or taking away from “the words of the prophecy of this book” (vv. 18–19). Like Moses' warning in Deuteronomy, it guards the message against the distortions of false prophets. It refers first to Revelation itself, but it shows how seriously God takes every word He has spoken.

And finally, “He who testifies these things says, ‘Yes, I come quickly.’ Amen! Yes, come, Lord Jesus” (v. 20). The church's last prayer is the prayer of the first Christians: Maranatha — ‘Come, Lord!’ (1 Corinthians 16:22). Paul speaks of “all those who have loved his appearing” (2 Timothy 4:8). The Bible ends not with a full stop but with a longing and a promise — and then with grace: “The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ be with all the saints. Amen” (v. 21).

ntConnection.heading: The Blessed Hope
paragraphs: Paul calls Christ's return “the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ” (Titus 2:13), and says the crown of righteousness is stored up “not to me only, but also to all those who have loved his appearing” (2 Timothy 4:8).

The face-to-face vision of verse 4 is the fulfilment of Paul's hope: “For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part, but then I will know fully, even as I was also fully known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

The church's prayer, ‘Come, Lord Jesus’, is the Greek form of the Aramaic Maranatha with which Paul closed his first letter to the Corinthians: “If any man doesn’t love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be accursed. Come, Lord!” (1 Corinthians 16:22). From the first generation to the last, the church has prayed it.

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “attendance (specially, medical, i.e. cure); figuratively and collectively, domestics.” θεραπεία, from θεραπεύω, gives us ‘therapy’. In the Gospels it describes Jesus' healing ministry. The leaves of the tree of life are ‘for the healing of the nations’: not because sickness exists in the new creation, but because all the wounds of history — between peoples, cultures and nations — will be fully and finally healed. Ezekiel's river had trees whose ‘leaf for healing’ never withered.

Strong's: “an imprecation.” κατανάθεμα (or κατάθεμα) is a curse, something devoted to destruction. After the first sin, God said, ‘Cursed is the ground for your sake.’ Paul says Christ redeemed us from the curse ‘having become a curse for us’ (Galatians 3:13). Because He bore the curse on the cross, ‘There will be no curse any more’ in the new creation. The story that began with a curse ends without one.

Strong's: “pertaining to the dawn, i.e. matutinal.” πρωϊνός describes the early morning, the first light. ‘The Bright and Morning Star’ is the planet Venus, which shines brightest just before sunrise, heralding the day. Jesus promised the overcomer in Thyatira, ‘I will give him the morning star’ (2:28); here He reveals that the star is Himself. In the darkest hour before dawn, He is the sign that the day is coming.

Strong's: “shortly, i.e. without delay, soon, or (by surprise) suddenly, or (by implication, of ease) readily.” ταχύ appears three times in Jesus' final words: ‘I come quickly’ (vv. 7, 12, 20). Strong's notes both ‘soon’ and ‘suddenly’. Two thousand years later, His coming is still ‘soon’ in God's time (2 Peter 3:8) and will certainly be sudden, like a thief. Every generation is to live as though He may come today.

Strong's: “to remove (literally or figuratively).” ἀφαιρέω means to take away or remove. Revelation ends with a warning modelled on Deuteronomy 4:2: ‘You shall not add to the word which I command you, neither shall you take away from it.’ Whoever adds to the book will receive its plagues; whoever takes away from it will lose their share in the tree of life. The book that reveals Jesus must be received whole — not edited to suit our tastes.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this final chapter the Holy Spirit and the bride join in one word: Come.

items.title: You Will See His Face
items.body: “They will see his face” (v. 4). The Spirit wants this hope to shape your whole life. One day you will look into the face of God and the Lamb. Live today as someone who is going to see Him.

items.title: Worship God
items.body: Even at the end, John needed to be reminded: “Worship God” (v. 9). The Spirit asks you to keep returning to the centre: not visions, not experiences, not leaders, not even angels, but God alone.

items.title: Say ‘Come’
items.body: “The Spirit and the bride say, ‘Come!’” (v. 17). The Spirit invites you to pray for Christ's return with longing — ‘Come, Lord Jesus’ — and to say ‘Come’ to every thirsty person you know, offering them the water of life freely.

audit.title: The Longing Check
audit.body: Do you long for Christ's return, or are you comfortable enough here that you would rather He waited (v. 20)?

audit.title: The Invitation Check
audit.body: Who in your life is thirsty and needs to hear ‘Come’ (v. 17)? When will you tell them?

audit.title: The Word Check
audit.body: Are there parts of God's word you would like to add to or take away from because they are uncomfortable (vv. 18–19)?

practices.title: Pray Maranatha
practices.body: Each morning and evening this week, pray the last prayer of the Bible: ‘Amen. Come, Lord Jesus.’ Then pray the last blessing for someone else: ‘The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.’

practices.title: Give Someone a Drink
practices.body: Invite one person this week to ‘come and drink’ — to read a Gospel with you, come to church, or hear your story of how Jesus satisfied your thirst. Offer it freely, as God offers it to you (v. 17).

prayerReflection: “Lord Jesus, You are the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End, the root and offspring of David, the bright morning star. Thank You for the river of the water of life flowing from Your throne, and for the tree of life whose leaves will heal the nations. Thank You that there will be no more curse, because You became a curse for me. I long to see Your face. Put Your name on my forehead. Be my light, so that there is no night in me. Keep me faithful to the words of this book. Teach me to worship God alone. Thank You that the water of life is free; I come and drink, and I want to bring others to drink with me. Your grace has carried me through this whole book, from the throne to the river. The Spirit and the bride say, ‘Come.’ I say it too: Amen. Come, Lord Jesus. The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all Your people. Amen.”

storyConnections.title: The Garden and the Tree of Life
storyConnections.summary: God planted a garden in Eden, with a river flowing out to water it and the tree of life in the middle. When Adam and Eve sinned, God drove them out and placed cherubim with a flaming sword to guard the way to the tree of life. For the rest of the Bible, the way back to the tree is closed — until Revelation 22, where the tree of life stands open on both sides of the river, in the middle of the city, and the curse is gone. The Bible's story ends where it began, but far better.

storyConnections.title: Ezekiel's River
storyConnections.summary: In his vision of the restored temple, Ezekiel saw water flowing out from under the threshold, growing from ankle-deep to knee-deep to a river too deep to cross. Wherever it flowed, it brought life: the Dead Sea became fresh and teemed with fish. On both banks grew trees whose leaves did not wither and whose fruit came every month, ‘and its leaf for healing’. Revelation 22 fulfils this vision in the new creation: the river of life from the throne, and the tree whose leaves heal the nations.

storyConnections.title: Moses Asks to See God's Glory
storyConnections.summary: After the golden calf, Moses pleaded with God, ‘Please show me your glory.’ God answered that He would make His goodness pass before him and proclaim His name, ‘but you cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.’ He hid Moses in a cleft of the rock and covered him with His hand as He passed by. In Revelation 22, what Moses could not have is given to all God's servants: ‘They will see his face.’
